transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, the main reason I’m here is that work is just... it's getting really hard. I'm a registered nurse, and on the floor I just lose my train of thought constantly. Like, an IV pump will beep, or a call light goes off down the hall, or even if I just hear someone asking another nurse a question, suddenly I’ve completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was working on. It's so frustrating. 

Actually, speaking of IV pumps, we just got these new ones on our unit last month, and the alarm tone is this horrible, high-pitched screech. It sounds exactly like the smoke detector in my apartment. My landlord was supposed to come fix that last week because it goes off every time I make toast, even if the bread isn't burning. I buy that thick sourdough from the bakery down the street, and it always gets stuck in the slots of my toaster... um, wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, I just... I keep losing my focus and forgetting what I'm doing with all the interruptions at the hospital.
Did you have similar problems with attention or distractibility when you were a child?

Yeah, actually, it's always been kind of a mess. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright but just really careless. I was constantly losing my worksheets or totally forgetting to turn in my homework. Which is funny, because I actually loved getting worksheets back then, especially the ones printed on that old mimeograph machine paper. Do you remember that stuff? With the purple ink that smelled really sweet? 

I actually bought a perfume a few weeks ago that smells exactly like it. It's from this little indie brand I found on Instagram, but the shipping took absolutely forever because the post office routed it to the wrong state. I had to call customer service three times, and their hold music is just this awful, tinny jazz loop that plays the same four notes over and over, and the lady on the phone was so unhelpful... um. Wait. Why was I talking about the post office? 

Oh! Right, school. Yeah, so because I kept losing all those worksheets and forgetting my assignments, my mom basically had to sit with me at the kitchen table every single night just to keep me on track. Otherwise, I'd just drift off and nothing would ever get finished.
Do you feel anxious or worried most of the time?

Anxious? Um, no, not really. I don't think I'm a worrier. I mean, I get stressed out, obviously, just because the floor is so chaotic, but it's not like a constant anxiety or dread. It's more just... being exhausted. 

Actually, speaking of being exhausted, I tried to buy these new compression socks the other day because my legs just ache so badly after a twelve-hour shift. I went to this little uniform shop right across from the hospital, but they were completely out of my size in all the fun patterns. They only had plain white, and white gets dirty so incredibly fast. Just on Tuesday, I spilled coffee all over my white scrub top. It was an iced caramel macchiato, which I know I shouldn't even be drinking because of the sugar, but the barista at the drive-thru always gives me extra caramel drizzle. She has this really adorable dog that sits in the window of the coffee shop, too. I think it's a goldendoodle? Or maybe a cockapoo. It has those little floppy curly ears and it always barks at the espresso machine... um. 

Wait. Sorry, I completely lost my train of thought again. What did you ask me? Something about work?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you felt down, sad, or depressed most days?

No, I wouldn't say I've felt down or depressed or anything like that. I mean, I get frustrated with myself for forgetting things, but I'm not sad. 

Actually, speaking of being sad, my sister called me crying the other night because her favorite TV show got canceled. It was one of those reality baking shows, the ones where they have to make these huge, elaborate cakes that look like everyday objects? I honestly don't get the appeal. Why would I want to eat a cake that looks exactly like a dirty sneaker or a potted plant? I tried to make a regular chocolate cake for my roommate's birthday last month, but I completely forgot I had put it in the oven because I started organizing my spice rack. I bought all these matching little glass jars with the bamboo lids, and I was printing out these tiny little labels on my label maker. The label maker is so cool, it connects to an app on my phone, but the bluetooth connection is really spotty. Sometimes it just drops right in the middle of printing, and then half the label is just blank... 

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? Um, you asked about being depressed, right? Yeah, no, I don't feel sad or depressed most days. Just... scattered.
Were you already having these attention and forgetfulness problems before age 12?

Before age 12? Um, I'm really bad with exact ages, to be honest. But like I was saying before, it was definitely happening back in elementary school, so yeah, I think so? I guess 12 would be around... sixth grade? Middle school? 

Middle school was a complete nightmare because that's when we suddenly had lockers. I could never, ever remember my locker combination. It was one of those heavy metal dial locks? I actually dropped mine right on my big toe once in the locker room before gym class. Gym class was the absolute worst. We had to wear these horrible, stiff polyester uniform shorts that were so itchy. I actually just bought my niece some shorts for her summer camp, but I got them at Target and they're this really soft, nice moisture-wicking material. Target has such dangerous aisles right now. I went in there on Sunday just to buy toothpaste and somehow ended up leaving with a whole outdoor patio set. It was on clearance, but I had to borrow my neighbor's truck to get it home, and his truck smells exactly like wet dog and old french fries... um. 

Wait. Sorry. Did I answer your question? You were asking about middle school, right?
Do these attention problems also happen outside of work, for example at home or in other parts of your life?

Oh, absolutely. It's definitely not just at the hospital. At home, I forget things that should be completely routine. Like, I'll totally forget to call a family member back, or pay a bill, or show up for an appointment. It happens even when I fully meant to do it, and sometimes even after I set a reminder on my phone! 

Like, just the other day I was supposed to follow up on a missing order. I bought these new blackout curtains because sleeping during the day after a night shift is impossible without them. The package just never arrived, so I set an alarm to call customer service. But when the alarm went off, my cat was throwing up a hairball on my living room rug. It's this vintage Persian rug I got at a flea market last summer. The guy selling it was so nice, he actually gave me a huge discount because it started pouring rain while I was looking at it. I love flea markets, but you have to get there super early if you want the good stuff, like by 6 AM. Which is basically when I'm just getting off my shift, so instead of going, I usually just grab a breakfast sandwich from this food truck that parks near the hospital. They make their own hot sauce from scratch, and it is incredibly spicy. I actually burned my tongue on it last week and couldn't taste anything for two days... 

Um. Wait, sorry. I'm rambling again. What were we just talking about? Oh, right, being at home. Yeah, so I just forget routine stuff all the time, even with reminders.
When you lose focus, is it usually because your mind is filled with worries or what-ifs?

No, it's not really worries or anything like that. I don't sit there thinking about bad things that could happen or stressing over what-ifs. It's more like my brain just... wanders off. Like, a thought pops into my head, and then I just follow it. 

Actually, speaking of wandering off, my parents used to have this golden retriever when I was a kid who would do exactly that. His name was Barnaby, and if you left the front door open even a crack, he would just trot right out and go on an adventure. We'd always find him like three blocks away, sitting on someone's porch just waiting for a treat. My dad got so fed up with it that he installed this really complicated deadbolt lock on the door. It was one of those smart locks that you can open with your fingerprint? But my dad's fingerprints are super worn down because he does so much woodworking in his garage. He builds these incredible birdhouses, like, really elaborate ones with little tiny shingles on the roof. He actually tried to sell them at a craft fair once, but it rained the entire weekend and the tent they set up completely collapsed under the water weight...

Wait, sorry. Did I answer the question? You were asking about worrying, right? Yeah, no, I don't really get stuck on worries or what-ifs. My mind just kind of goes its own way.
Have you ever had a head injury, concussion, stroke, or other brain condition that started these attention problems?

No, nothing like that. I've never hit my head or had a concussion or anything. I mean, I've had some clumsy moments, but nothing that involved my head. 

Actually, speaking of being clumsy, I did sprain my ankle really badly last winter. I was walking out to my car after a shift and slipped on this patch of black ice in the employee parking lot. The hospital is supposed to salt the walkways, but they always miss this one spot right near the staff entrance. It's so frustrating. I had to wear one of those giant walking boots for like six weeks. The worst part was trying to drive with it. I have a manual transmission—it's a little Honda Civic I bought used from my cousin. He takes really good care of his cars, always gets the oil changed exactly on time and everything. He's an accountant, so he's super meticulous about numbers and schedules. I actually need to text him back about his birthday dinner this weekend. We're supposed to go to this new Italian place downtown that makes their own pasta. I love fresh pasta, especially when they do that thing where they mix it in a giant cheese wheel right at your table... 

Um, sorry. I lost my train of thought again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, head injuries. Yeah, no, I've never had a stroke or a concussion or anything wrong with my brain like that.
Do you also have trouble remembering recent events or conversations, or is it mainly losing focus and getting distracted?

No, I don't really have trouble remembering conversations or things that just happened. It's definitely more about just losing my focus. Like, if someone tells me a story, I can remember the story perfectly fine, assuming I was actually paying attention when they told it. 

Which, honestly, is the hard part. Like my friend Sarah, she was telling me this long story the other day about her garden. She decided to plant all these heirloom tomatoes this year. She bought the seeds online from this specialty farm in Oregon, I think? They're supposed to be these really beautiful purple and green striped tomatoes. But she has this huge problem with squirrels getting into her yard. They just wait until the tomatoes are perfectly ripe and then take exactly one bite out of each one. It's so mean! She tried putting up this wire fencing, but squirrels are practically acrobats. I saw a video once of a squirrel doing an entire obstacle course just to get to a bird feeder. It was like Ninja Warrior but for rodents. They had to jump over spinning logs and swing from tiny ropes... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, remembering things. Yeah, my memory is fine! It's just staying focused in the moment that's the problem.
Have these attention problems gotten noticeably worse compared with how you used to function a few years ago?

Well, I wouldn't say they've gotten worse out of nowhere, but it's definitely been a major problem since I took on the expanded charge-nurse responsibilities almost two years ago. It's just so much more to juggle now. 

Actually, speaking of juggling, one of the new nurses on my floor used to be in a circus arts program before she went to nursing school. Isn't that wild? She can literally juggle fire batons. She showed us a video on her phone during our lunch break last week. She was wearing this incredible sparkly costume with sequins all over it. I love sequins, but they are so hard to wash. I had this sequin top I wore to a New Year's Eve party once, and I accidentally put it in the dryer instead of letting it air dry. It completely melted half the sequins together into this weird plastic clump. I was so upset because I bought it at this vintage boutique downtown that always has the best stuff. The owner is this older woman named Beatrice who has the most amazing collection of antique brooches. She told me once that she finds them at estate sales...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um, you were asking if things got worse? Yeah, it's just been really hard to keep up since I got the charge-nurse role a couple of years ago.
Did these attention problems start after any specific illness, injury, or other medical event?

No, I don't think so. I mean, there wasn't any big sickness or anything that happened right before all this started. I've been pretty healthy, mostly. 

Well, I did have a really bad case of the flu maybe four years ago? It was right around Thanksgiving. I was supposed to make the sweet potato casserole for my family's dinner, and I had already bought all the ingredients. I use this special recipe that my grandmother gave me—it has pecans and brown sugar on top instead of marshmallows. I really don't like marshmallows on sweet potatoes, they just get too sticky and sweet. Anyway, I was so sick I couldn't even get out of bed, let alone cook. My sister had to take over, and she completely ruined it. She burned the pecans because she forgot to set a timer. She's always doing things like that. She's a graphic designer, so she gets super absorbed in her computer screen and just loses track of time completely. She designed the logo for this local coffee shop near my apartment, actually. It's a really cute place, they have these amazing lavender lattes...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, illnesses. Yeah, no, the attention stuff didn't start after an illness or anything like that. It's just kind of always been there, but got way worse with the new job responsibilities.
Before these attention problems started, did you ever have a period where your concentration and organization were completely normal?

Normal? Um, no, honestly, I don't think I've ever had a time where I was completely put together like that. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was constantly losing my worksheets or just completely forgetting to turn in my homework once I'd finished it. 

I remember this one time in fourth grade, we had to do this project on the solar system, and I made this incredible diorama in a shoebox. My mom helped me paint little styrofoam balls for the planets, and we used this silver glitter paint for the stars. The glitter got absolutely everywhere. My mom was vacuuming it out of the living room rug for months! It's crazy how glitter never really goes away, you know? Like, I bought a birthday card for my niece last month that had glitter on it, and I'm still finding specks of it on my car seats. She just turned five, and my sister rented this massive bouncy castle for her party. I actually went in it for a few minutes, which was a terrible idea because I had just eaten a huge piece of ice cream cake. They got the cake from that bakery downtown, the one with the pink awning? They make the absolute best buttercream frosting... 

Wait, sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. What was I... oh, right, school. Yeah, so I would do all this homework and then just leave it sitting on the kitchen table. My mom actually had to sit with me every single night just to keep me on track and make sure my worksheets actually made it into my folder. So, yeah, I've never really been naturally organized.
Do you also tend to feel physically restless or fidgety, like you have trouble sitting still?

Um, physically restless? No, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I have to be running around or anything. I can sit still just fine. 

Actually, sitting still is basically my favorite thing to do when I get home from a shift. I have this amazing recliner in my living room. It's one of those oversized, super plush ones? I found it on sale at this furniture outlet out by the highway. It was such a steal because there was a tiny scratch on the back leg, but you can't even see it because it's pushed up against the wall. I always sit there with my cat, Barnaby. He's a Maine Coon mix, so he's absolutely massive, like twenty pounds of pure fluff. He sheds like crazy, though. I have to buy those sticky lint rollers in bulk from Costco. Costco is so dangerous, honestly. I went in there last week just for lint rollers and paper towels, and I walked out with a giant tub of chocolate-covered almonds and a new set of mixing bowls. The bowls were such a pretty teal color, I just couldn't resist. I've been wanting to try making my own sourdough bread, and I figured they'd be perfect for that. Everyone was making sourdough during the pandemic, but I was working so many shifts at the hospital I never had time to even think about baking...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um, no, I don't really get fidgety or feel like I can't sit still. It's more just my brain that won't sit still, you know?
Have you noticed any problems with the orientation of memory, like getting lost in familiar places or mixing up where you are, that are new for you?

Getting lost? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I know my way around the hospital and my neighborhood just fine. I haven't been mixing up places or anything like that. 

Although, speaking of getting lost, my friend Sarah just got back from a trip to Italy and she said she got completely turned around in Venice. Apparently, the streets there are like a total maze, and Google Maps doesn't even work right because the buildings are so close together. She said she spent like two hours trying to find this one specific gelato place that she saw on TikTok. She finally found it, but she said the pistachio flavor wasn't even that good. Which is a shame, because pistachio is my absolute favorite. There's this little Italian place downtown that makes their own pistachio gelato, and it's incredible. They serve it in these tiny glass cups with a little silver spoon. I went there for my birthday last year with a bunch of girls from my unit. We had such a good time, but the parking downtown is just a nightmare. I ended up having to park in this garage that was like six blocks away, and it cost me twenty dollars just for a few hours. It's ridiculous how much they charge for parking now...

Oh, wait. Sorry. No, I haven't been getting lost or forgetting where I am. Just the normal spacing out stuff.
Have you always been this distractible and forgetful, or is this a newer change for you?

Well, like I said, I was always kind of a space cadet when I was younger, but it's gotten so much worse lately. This has really been a major problem since I took on the expanded charge-nurse responsibilities almost two years ago. 

Being a charge nurse is just... it's a lot. You have to juggle so many things at once. And the hospital has been so short-staffed lately, it's just exhausting. We had three nurses call out on my unit just last Tuesday. Tuesday is usually my easy day, too, because they usually schedule me with Sarah, and we just have this great rhythm working together. She's the one who went to Italy, actually. She brought me back this beautiful leather coin purse from Florence. It's this deep burgundy color, and it smells amazing. I love the smell of real leather. It reminds me of this jacket my dad used to wear when I was a kid. He had this old motorcycle, a Harley, I think? He used to take me for rides around the neighborhood on Sunday afternoons. We'd always stop at the Dairy Queen at the end of our street. They tore that Dairy Queen down a few years ago to build a bank, which is so depressing. I mean, who even goes into a physical bank anymore? Everything is on your phone now. I have like three different banking apps on my phone, and I still can't remember my passwords for half of them. I always have to click the 'forgot password' link and then wait for the email...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, if this is new. Yeah, so, I've always been a little scattered, but it really blew up into a huge issue when I got promoted two years ago and had to manage all those extra duties. It's just too much to keep track of now.
Have you had any significant change in your sense of smell?

My sense of smell? No, I haven't noticed anything weird with that. Everything smells normal. 

I actually have a really good sense of smell, which is honestly a curse sometimes working at the hospital. You wouldn't believe the smells on a med-surg floor. The other day, someone brought in this fish dish for the breakroom microwave, and it just lingered for hours. I don't know why people think it's okay to microwave fish in a shared space. It's like an unwritten rule, right? Kind of like how you shouldn't wear strong perfume to work. There used to be this nurse on the night shift who wore this incredibly heavy floral perfume, and you could tell exactly which rooms she had been in just by the smell. It reminded me of my grandmother's house. She used to have all these little glass bottles of perfume on her vanity, and she'd let me play with them when I visited. She lived in this old Victorian house that always smelled like potpourri and lemon pledge. I loved that house. My cousins and I used to play hide-and-seek in the attic, which was probably super dangerous because there were all these old exposed nails and floorboards that felt like they were going to cave in...

Anyway, um, no. No changes in my sense of smell. It's totally fine.
Have you noticed your overall ability to function getting progressively worse over the past few years?

Yeah, it really has. I mean, at work, things have gotten so bad that I'm actually on formal supervision now. They have other nurses double-checking parts of my charge-nurse follow-through, which is just... it's so humiliating. I feel like I'm becoming a liability instead of a leader. 

It reminds me of when I was in nursing school, and we had this one clinical instructor, Mrs. Gable. She was so strict, she used to follow us around with a literal clipboard and check off every single step we did when we were doing a sterile dressing change. I was always so nervous around her that my hands would shake, and I almost dropped a sterile Q-tip once. She gave me this look that could freeze water. I actually ran into her a few years ago at the grocery store, of all places. She was buying like, ten bags of potting soil. I guess she's really into gardening now. I tried to get into gardening during the pandemic, you know, when everyone was growing sourdough starters and planting tomatoes? I bought all these expensive raised beds and heirloom seeds, but I kept forgetting to water them, so everything just shriveled up and died. The only thing that survived was this one rogue zucchini plant that grew to the size of a baseball bat. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, makes this amazing zucchini bread, so I gave it to him. He's such a sweet old man, he always brings my mail up to the porch if it's raining...

But, um, yeah, sorry. My ability to function is definitely getting worse. The supervision at work is a huge wake-up call.
Do you remember having any attention or organization problems before elementary school?

Before elementary school? Um, I don't really remember much from before then, to be honest. But I definitely know it was an issue once I started school. Even in elementary school, my teachers were always writing on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was constantly losing my worksheets or just completely forgetting to turn in my homework. 

My mom actually had to sit with me at the kitchen table every single night just to keep me on track so I'd actually finish anything. We had this big oak table, it was super heavy. My dad bought it at an estate sale before I was born. He loved going to estate sales and auctions. He'd always come home with the most random stuff, like a box of vintage doorknobs or a collection of antique spoons. We had this one spoon that had a tiny little windmill on the handle, and the blades actually spun. I used to love playing with it when I was supposed to be eating my cereal. I was a really picky eater as a kid, I basically only ate Cheerios and those little frozen waffle things. The ones you put in the toaster? I burned my fingers on the toaster once because I tried to pull the waffle out before it popped up. I still have a tiny little scar on my thumb from it. It's barely noticeable, but I know it's there. It's kind of funny how scars stick around forever, you know? Like, your body just never forgets...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, school. Yeah, so, I was definitely losing things and forgetting homework all the way back in elementary school, and my mom had to basically force me to focus.
Before age 12, were you already having these attention or organization problems?

Yeah, like I was just saying, it was definitely happening back then. I was always losing my worksheets or completely forgetting to turn in my homework, even in elementary school. My teachers would always write on my report cards that I was "bright but careless." That phrase is practically burned into my brain. 

My mom had to sit with me at the kitchen table every single night just to keep me on track so I'd actually finish my assignments. She was so patient, honestly. She'd make us this chamomile tea with honey while we worked. She always bought the honey from this local guy at the farmer's market who kept bees in his backyard. He had this big bushy beard and always wore overalls, like a stereotypical lumberjack or something. I always wondered if he ever got stung. I got stung by a bee once when I was like seven, right on the bottom of my foot. I was running through the clover in our backyard barefoot, which my dad always told me not to do. He was so particular about the lawn. He used to spend every Saturday morning out there with the edger, making sure the lines along the driveway were perfectly straight. It drove him crazy when the dandelions popped up. He'd go out there with this special tool just to dig them out by the root... 

But yeah, before I was 12, I was definitely having those same problems with losing things and needing my mom to basically force me to focus on my homework.
Have you been forgetting things that you would normally remember, like recent conversations or events?

Yeah, all the time. It's like my brain just drops things that should be completely routine. I'll forget to call my sister back, or at work I'll forget to follow up on a missing order for a patient. I even forget to pay bills at home or show up for appointments, even when I fully meant to do it and, like, actually set a reminder on my phone. 

My phone is basically just a very expensive alarm clock at this point. I have the ringtone set to this classical music piece, I think it's Vivaldi? Because I read somewhere that classical music is supposed to be less jarring for your nervous system when you wake up. I used to have it set to this really loud, obnoxious buzzer sound, but it would scare my cat, Barnaby, half to death every morning. He's a rescue, a big orange tabby, and he's super skittish. The shelter said they found him hiding under a dumpster behind a seafood restaurant. I guess that's why he goes absolutely crazy whenever I open a can of tuna. I try to only buy the sustainably caught kind, you know, because of the dolphins. I watched this documentary once about the ocean and it just broke my heart, all that plastic floating around... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, forgetting things. Yeah, routine things just slip right out of my head, even with reminders. It's really frustrating.

Yeah, actually, it's always been kind of a mess. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright but just really careless. I was constantly losing my worksheets or totally forgetting to turn in my homework. Which is funny, because I actually loved getting worksheets back then, especially the ones printed on that old mimeograph machine paper. Do you remember that stuff? With the purple ink that smelled really sweet? 

I actually bought a perfume a few weeks ago that smells exactly like it. It's from this little indie brand I found on Instagram, but the shipping took absolutely forever because the post office routed it to the wrong state. I had to call customer service three times, and their hold music is just this awful, tinny jazz loop that plays the same four notes over and over, and the lady on the phone was so unhelpful... um. Wait. Why was I talking about the post office? 

Oh! Right, school. Yeah, so because I kept losing all those worksheets and forgetting my assignments, my mom basically had to sit with me at the kitchen table every single night just to keep me on track. Otherwise, I'd just drift off and nothing would ever get finished.

doctor.intent: To determine whether the inattention is primarily due to anxiety rather than lifelong ADHD or another condition.
doctor.question: Do you feel anxious or worried most of the time?

patient.answer:
Anxious? Um, no, not really. I don't think I'm a worrier. I mean, I get stressed out, obviously, just because the floor is so chaotic, but it's not like a constant anxiety or dread. It's more just... being exhausted. 

Actually, speaking of being exhausted, I tried to buy these new compression socks the other day because my legs just ache so badly after a twelve-hour shift. final_diagnosis.reason: The interview is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation, with longstanding symptoms beginning in childhood, persistence into adulthood, impairment across work and home, and no evidence of a head injury, stroke, or other medical condition causing the attention problems. She denies depressed mood, constant anxiety, psychotic symptoms, or prominent recent-onset cognitive decline, making F06.7 less likely.
